clue.text: I have 10 to eat

parts.note: the figures 1 and 0 are read as the letters I and O
to eat is to dine

explanation.surface: Someone announces they have ten guests coming round to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: In this element puzzle each chemical symbol is a definition: I is the symbol of the element. The '10' is read as its look-alike letters I and O; 'have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical symbol stands for the halogen element used as an antiseptic.

clue.text: Most foul devil's turn with the others

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
a U-turn, so U stands for a turn
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A wicked devil takes a turn alongside the remaining people.
explanation.walkthrough: U stands for a turn, as in U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Impurest is the superlative of impure, meaning dirtiest or most tainted.

clue.text: A handful of dust by Cicero, if included in the prescribed manner

indicators.note: by means next to, so the letters sit beside the rest
a handful is a small part, so only a couple of letters of the word dust are taken
included signals that the little word if goes inside the orator's name

parts.note: Tully is the old English name for Marcus Tullius Cicero

explanation.surface: A Roman orator includes a pinch of dust in some rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A handful of' takes just a couple of letters from 'dust'. Cicero was traditionally called Tully in English; 'included' puts the second piece inside that name, and 'by' sets the first beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something dutifully means doing it as duty or rules require.

clue.text: Feature heard to be opposed to the eyes

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is identified by its sound

parts.words: to be opposed to the eyes
parts.note: in a parliamentary vote the noes oppose the ayes, which sound like eyes

explanation.surface: A face part said to be at odds with the eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyes' sounds like 'ayes', the yes voters in Parliament; those against them are the NOES.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is one of the parts of the face, which are called features.

clue.text: F for uranium in old coin (English)

indicators.note: the uranium symbol is placed inside the coin's name

parts.note: a florin was the old British two-shilling piece
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A recipe swapping one letter for uranium inside an old English coin.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the element's symbol. FLORIN was a British coin worth two shillings, withdrawn after decimalisation; 'in' puts U between its L and O.
explanation.definitionFit: F is the chemical symbol of the pale yellow halogen gas added to toothpaste.

clue.text: One piece of sugar on another, a thousand paid all at once

annotationWithheld.why: One piece of sugar on another, a thousand paid all at once (4,3): LUMP + SU + M needs 'sugar' twice, as the piece giving LUMP and as the source of SU
annotationWithheld.clue: One piece of sugar on another, a thousand paid all at once

clue.text: Request for quiet at home during excursion, putting in the shade

indicators.note: the two short pieces fall within the word for an excursion

parts.note: an outing is an excursion
sh is the noise asking for quiet
in means at home

explanation.surface: Asking for silence at home in the middle of a day trip, overshadowing everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts the two short pieces inside the excursion word; 'Request for quiet' is the shushing sound, not a polite ask.
explanation.definitionFit: Outshining someone is surpassing them so they look lesser, eclipsing them.

clue.text: Put in the ground with something on either side?

explanation.surface: Burying something with something on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury; and the prefix inter- means between, which is something with neighbours either side.

clue.text: The royal shilling, I take it, is io when changed

annotationWithheld.why: The royal shilling, I take it, is io when changed (6): 'io' is garbled and the anagram fodder for ENLIST is missing
annotationWithheld.clue: The royal shilling, I take it, is io when changed

clue.text: Lady with intelligence will fade away

parts.note: wit is intelligence, quickness of mind
her refers to a lady

explanation.surface: A woman of brains will lose her bloom one day.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts are WIT and HER; 'Lady' supplies HER, and 'with' places it beside WIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel and droop, as a plant does.

clue.text: K takes a drug, the fool, before hesitating first

indicators.note: the clue's order says the piece for first goes ahead of the hesitation sound

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, a drug
an ass is a fool
first is number one, written as the Roman numeral I
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drug, plays the fool, and hesitates before going first.
explanation.walkthrough: K is the symbol of the element (from Latin kalium). 'before hesitating first' tells you to put I (one, first) ahead of UM.
explanation.definitionFit: K is the chemical symbol of the soft reactive metal found in bananas.

clue.text: Destroy the lot

explanation.surface: An order to wreck everything in sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To write off a vehicle completely is informally to wreck it; and a grand sum counts everything, all of it.

clue.text: A bird round one's neck, maybe winning trick

explanation.surface: A bird, maybe wearing something round its neck, plays a winning card.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpiper whose male grows a frilled collar; an Elizabethan pleated collar; and in whist or bridge, trumping a card to take the trick.

clue.text: P to page half the medical centre and a god

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for a medical centre is kept

parts.note: a hospital is a medical centre
Horus is the falcon-headed god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: An instruction to page someone at the hospital, perhaps a god.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the symbol of the element. 'half' keeps HOSP, the first four of the eight letters of HOSPITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: P is the chemical symbol of the glowing non-metal used in matches.

clue.text: Biblical records made by honourable clerics

indicators.note: made by signals the letters are reassembled from the pieces that follow

parts.note: Hon is the abbreviation for Honourable, as in a title

explanation.surface: Bible histories written by worthy churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: HON plus CLERICS are rearranged; 'made by' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronicles is the name of two Old Testament books of history.

clue.text: S, as Fiennes ran away, is almost certain to go without

indicators.note: the clipped word for certain goes on the outside of the explorer's trimmed name
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: certain means sure

indicators.note: away tells us the letters of the word ran are taken off the name

parts.note: Sir Ranulph Fiennes is the British polar explorer
the clue word ran is taken as written

explanation.surface: Explorer Fiennes has run off, so the certain thing must go without him.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the symbol of the element. RANULPH loses RAN, leaving ULPH, which sits inside SUR (SURE with 'almost' dropping its E). 'Fiennes' suggests the actor Ralph; it is the explorer Ranulph.
explanation.definitionFit: S is the chemical symbol of the yellow non-metal once called brimstone.

clue.text: Lament the moment when Enid Blyton character lost heart

parts.note: mo is short for moment, as in 'half a mo'

indicators.note: the middle letter of the five-letter name is removed

parts.note: Noddy is the little wooden toy boy in Enid Blyton's children's books

explanation.surface: A sad song for the day a children's book hero became discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: NODDY has five letters; 'lost heart' drops the middle one, a D, leaving NODY.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is a mourning poem or song sung by one voice, a dirge.

clue.text: D of French wombs? I'm not sure

parts.note: de is French for of
uteri is the plural of uterus, a womb
um is a sound expressing uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over a French phrase about wombs.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the symbol of this heavy isotope of hydrogen. UTERI is the Latin plural of uterus.
explanation.definitionFit: D is the chemical symbol for heavy hydrogen, used in nuclear reactors.

clue.text: H has information on health resort

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed below, so the information follows the resort

parts.note: a hydro is a spa hotel offering water treatments
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone has the details on a spa.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the symbol of the element. A HYDRO is a British spa hotel; GEN is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: H is the chemical symbol of the lightest gas, first in the periodic table.

clue.text: Old boy genuine? Fake

indicators.note: something fake is made up, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: gen is information, the genuine facts, as in 'the real gen'

explanation.surface: Is this old boy genuine, or a fake?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fake' is the anagram signal, applied to BOY and GEN. 'Old boy' wants to be one piece, but 'Old' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bygone describes days past, things belonging to an earlier time.

clue.text: Biblical correspondence? Sleep it off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of sleep it are reordered

explanation.surface: Advice to sleep off something, perhaps a hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal for SLEEP IT. The question mark marks the definition as an example: one of Paul's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament epistles are letters from apostles to churches.

clue.text: Call about wrong tune recently finished

indicators.note: the word for a call goes around the rearranged tune

parts.note: to call out is to cry

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of tune are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone shouts about a tune played wrongly that has just ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the tune, and 'about' wraps the call around it. The definition refers to the hundred-year span that had just ended when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The twentieth century was the hundred-year period that had only just closed.

clue.text: C is good for transport copies available

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
bon is French for good

explanation.surface: Carbon copies are handy for anyone sending transport orders.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the symbol of the element. 'copies available' points to carbon copies, a second hint at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: C is the chemical symbol of the element in diamonds and graphite.

clue.text: French island or American county? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Hants is the short form of Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Is this a French island or an American county? Neither, quite.
explanation.walkthrough: HANTS is the usual short form for Hampshire, a county in southern England; 'Not quite' drops its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushant is the island off Brittany at the mouth of the English Channel.

clue.text: Is transport backed by record? Not the principal

indicators.note: backed means the joined words is and bus are read in reverse

parts.note: a bus is a form of transport
a diary is a daily record

explanation.surface: A question whether transport is supported by records, followed by a denial that it is the principal one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the 'Is' and the transport word round together as one unit; 'by' just sets the record beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A subsidiary company or role is secondary, subordinate to the main one.

clue.text: B is right in the present

indicators.note: the right abbreviation goes inside the word for a present

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing

explanation.surface: A remark that B is correct at the present time.
explanation.walkthrough: B is the symbol of the element. 'the present' suggests now, but it is a gift, BOON.
explanation.definitionFit: B is the chemical symbol of the metalloid found in borax.

clue.text: Beast to have a child

explanation.surface: A wild animal about to give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A large furry animal of the woods; and to give birth to offspring.

clue.text: A qualification to be a neighbour

parts.note: but introduces a qualification or reservation

explanation.surface: Someone needs a certificate before being allowed to live next door.
explanation.walkthrough: A BUT is a qualification in the sense of a reservation: 'no ifs or buts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two properties that abut touch along a boundary, adjoining each other.

clue.text: That chap Rilke has a bit of spring in him

indicators.note: has signals that the run of letters is held within the words chap Rilke

explanation.surface: The poet Rilke has some springtime about him.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'chAP RILke'; 'in him' rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month falls in the season of spring, so it is one part of it.

clue.text: Stroll around Irish city without leader, which is vexatious

indicators.note: the word for stroll is wrapped around the beheaded city

parts.note: to trog is British informal for to walk or tramp along

indicators.note: the first letter of the city's name is taken off

parts.note: Dublin is the capital of Ireland

explanation.surface: A walk round an Irish city with no guide proves irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: To trog is British slang for a trudging walk. 'without leader' beheads the Irish capital, and 'around' wraps the walk about what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troubling is worrying or annoying, causing distress.

clue.text: W to cross new gun with machine-gun…

parts.note: a tau cross is shaped like the letter T

indicators.note: new means the letters of gun are rearranged

parts.note: the Sten was a British submachine gun of the Second World War

explanation.surface: An order to cross-breed a new gun with a machine-gun.
explanation.walkthrough: W is the symbol of the element (from wolfram). 'new' rearranges GUN into UNG; 'to' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: W is the chemical symbol of the hard metal used in lamp filaments.

clue.text: … that's round in the morning with part of flower

indicators.note: the gun of the previous clue goes round the morning abbreviation

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on from the last clue, so that is the machine-gun, the Sten
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Continuing the gun story: that one is fired off in the morning near a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue, so 'that' is its machine-gun; 'round' wraps it about the morning abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing male organ of a flower.
